paragraphs: Citylogix sells municipal asset and work order management software, pitched at communities of every size. It also collects the data that feeds the software, driving streets with LiDAR and 360-degree imaging to map road conditions and right-of-way assets.

Inside the software, work orders are tied to the assets themselves and travel from the office to the crew and back. Machine learning grades pavement distress and turns it into heatmaps of the worst stretches. Sidewalk and ADA ramp condition assessment is offered alongside the road work. Budget and capital planning tools are meant to help a public works director justify what gets funded. Resident service requests drop into the same work order queue.

The customers are municipalities across North America. The company reports miles under management in 40 states, four provinces and one territory. It also counts ramps assessed for ADA and AODA compliance among its results. A recent announcement describes a partnership with NIRA Dynamics for continuous, IRI-based road monitoring using survey vehicles. The contact block lists an address on Salem Street in Wakefield, Massachusetts.
